title: Deep threads stay readable: 'continue this thread →' pages beyond five levels, and a collapse/expand toggle on every comment
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: No page (/, /reports/<slug>, a branch page) nests a comment more than five levels deep: missing
A depth-5 comment whose replies are cut shows a 'continue this thread →' link to /reports/<slug>/comments/<id>: missing

GET /reports/{slug}/comments/{id} opens that branch on its own page, with a link back to the full report and reply forms for a signed-in reader; hidden or unknown report, bad id or pruned id → the same 404: missing
A reply posted below the cap is answered 303 to the branch page that shows it (#comment-<id>), and to /reports/<slug>#comments if the re-read fails: missing
Every comment with shown replies has a collapse/expand toggle that, in a browser, hides and then shows everything beneath it, using /static/thread.js served from the site's own path: missing
Deep conversations stay readable on phones (the cut at five keeps a depth-5 comment body a usable width): missing
m7 (.toggle[hidden]{display:none}): waived to note N-066; .toggle sets no display, so the no-JS default holds.
m8 (Content-Type media type assertion in TestStaticThreadScript): waived to note N-067; the test checks the 200, the script body, the page tags and the raw CSP only.
The phone-width real-browser check is a runner mode (`look`) for validate, not a Go test; the Go test models the CSS arithmetic only.
Report to the person that the approved epics.finish body for test_e004_2 falls back to msedge.exe and ignores CHROME_BIN. The scratch runner guards it; the ledger body is untouched.
internal/server/harness_test.go was not gofmt-clean before this slice (struct field alignment); left as it was.
Q-012 (site JavaScript) stays open: thread.js is DOM-only and under the fitness fence, but it is now site JavaScript on the reader pages.
Validate should run `run_finish_e004_2.py look` itself and view the screenshots at 360 and 400 px; the unbroken-login control only shows if the viewer width is the one asked for.

deviation: TestReaderPathVariants: the existing row POST /reports/x/comments/extra changed from 404 to 405 Allow: GET, HEAD. The new GET /reports/{slug}/comments/{id} pattern also matches any single extra segment, so the mux answers a POST with 405 before any handler. The critique only checked the trailing-slash row. Routing was not changed to suit the test.

deviation: The critic's look prescribed `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`. Measured under mobile emulation it is blind: an overflowing page widens innerWidth too (572 of 572 without the login fix). The look compares scrollWidth to the width asked for.

deviation: A removed comment that has replies drawn below it also carries the toggle (the design says every comment with rendered replies), so TestCommentPlaceholders accepts 'comment removed Hide replies'. Case F of that test is rebuilt around the cap, because a depth-6 leaf is no longer on the report page. TestCommentLiteralHTML allows the one site script tag.
deviation: The first look seeded a 39-character login with a hyphen, which is a break point, so it was blind. It now uses 39 'w' characters.

deviation: A serve mode was added to the runner so the engine can open the new screens, because config refuses to start the app without HBAND_* variables (lesson #961). It reuses the finish test's Product class with a one-line port patch applied only in serve mode.

deviation: Waived by a person, so not built: m7 (.toggle[hidden] guard, N-066) and m8 (Content-Type assertion, N-067). The toggle rule has no display property, so the no-JS default stays hidden. No setting or notice was added: nothing here works around a defect outside this project (the Edge guard is a rule for the tests, and the login wrap is a layout fix).
